research_notes: The current strict sample uses a single scheduler writer and single authoritative worker, eliminating duplicate-authority ambiguity from the runtime measurement.
This is important because concurrent authoritative work could make a clean close appear successful while hiding side-effect duplication.
Parallelism will later require separate duplicate-work metrics and fencing.
Those concerns are intentionally absent from the current boundary evidence.
The sample therefore isolates runtime/close behavior more cleanly.
No control conflict has been observed.
